utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness's microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it for the interpretation

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If you'd like to take a seat. Yes, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Naumovski, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Before we start, two things, please. First of all, I would like to ask the Court to give two or three minutes to the Kordic Defence after we finish questioning the witnesses. We would like to familiarise the Court with two or three matters. Also, I wish to tell the Court that Mr. Arar came today because he wishes to testify, but he is still in not a very good condition, so I wish to ask the Honourable Judges to make it possible for Mr. Arar to leave the courtroom at some point if he feels so unwell, with your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Arar, we will try and see that this session is as short as possible. Do you feel well enough now to make a start? You'll have to speak up, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I feel well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. But if at any stage you don't feel well, just indicate and we can adjourn for a few moments. Mr. Naumovski, no doubt, with that in mind, you can take the matter as quickly as you can in order that the witness doesn't have to stay too long. Begin, if you would, with his full name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, could you please speak up, first and foremost, and please give us your name.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Ivo Arar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, you were born on the 19th of May, 1948 in Kiseljak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You are a Bosnian Croat by ethnicity and a Roman Catholic by religion?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You are a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: A few words about your schooling. You completed elementary school in Kiseljak and secondary school in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: After completing secondary school in 1968, you did your compulsory military service in the Yugoslav People's Army from 1968 to 1969?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: After completing your military service, you went to the Republic of Germany and you worked there for ten years, from 1970 to 1980?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You worked as a construction worker most of the time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: After that, about 1980, you returned to Kiseljak from Germany and started your own construction business, and you did that all the way up to 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Right now you live and work in the town of Knin in the Republic of Croatia, and you are working as a janitor in the club of the Croatian army in Knin?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, could you just wait for my questions to be interpreted first and then answer them, to make it easier for the interpreters. Mr. Arar, as for Mr. Ignac Kostroman, you've known him all your life; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When the HVO was just being organised -- oh, I do apologise. When the HDZ of Bosnia and Herzegovina was just being organised, Mr. Ignac Kostroman became the administrative secretary of the HDZ of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: As I said, this was after 1990, 1991, and you spent time with him, first when the establishment was being set up and then when you started working with him?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: After Sarajevo had been surrounded by the forces of the Bosnian Serb army, you returned from Sarajevo to Kiseljak; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: From that April 1992, when you returned to Kiseljak -- or rather, in April you became the escort and driver of Mr. Ignac Kostroman; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And you carried out these duties for almost two years, is that right, throughout the civil war, all the way up to March 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You were with Mr. Kostroman more or less all the time, except for when the Busovaca-Kiseljak road was cut off, and when in 1993 you were on the other side in Kiseljak and when it was impossible for you to return to Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: However, from the 24th of January, 1993, until the end of April 1993, that was the case, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: How did you return from Kiseljak to Tisovac? With whose assistance?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I returned with the help of UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Quite a bit of this time that Mr. Kostroman spent in Tisovac, you spent with him, and you are more or less familiar with the situation in that house where you also lived in Tisovac?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: During your stay there, you had the opportunity to see various political delegations coming in, delegations of political parties, et cetera; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I imagine they were not delegations of a single ethnic group only.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So we're talking about delegations of Serbs, Muslims, the International Community, et cetera; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, together with Kostroman, you lived in that same house, the former Vila Ivancica where Mr. Kostroman worked, and Mr. Kordic too. Tell me, how many people worked together with you doing various things?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: There was a total number of 14 persons who were working there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: That includes a comprehensive pattern of staff, doesn't it; cooks, drivers, guards, yourself included?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You were some kind of an office, weren't you? There was Mr. Kostroman, Mr. Kordic, and the 14 of you who helped them work; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell me, how should I call this group of people?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What kind of clothes did you wear?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: However, not everybody were soldiers?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell me, please, at that time, to the best of your knowledge, the headquarters of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade was originally located in the post office building in the town of Busovaca; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But later it was moved to another place.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, to the Sumarija building.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Is that also in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The office where Mr. Kostroman and Mr. Kordic worked, that is to say, of the HDZ and Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, did it ever have its headquarters either in Sumarija in Busovaca or in the post office building in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When you were there, especially after the summer of 1992, was this building where you were in Tisovac or the area around it, was it ever used as a military facility?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Kostroman -- I do apologise. Mr. Arar, have you ever heard of the Scorpions, a military unit known as the Scorpions?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of Mr. Kordic ever having had some kind of a role in selecting soldiers for any unit of the HVO, or of the military police, or of some special unit of a different nature?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You were there all the time, so you know Mr. Kordic. You know the basic duties that he performed while you were Mr. Kostroman's escort?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Honourable Court about this?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Dario Kordic held the office of one of the vice-presidents of the HZ HB, and he was one of the presidents of the Presidency of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You mean "vice-presidents"? You said "presidents".

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes, vice-presidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, don't lead the witness on matters which are or may be important. And the understanding of the role of Mr. Kordic is clearly an important issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. As far as Mr. Arar is concerned, this was a question put just in passing, so perhaps I could ask something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of an office Mr. Kordic held in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, because you talked about the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: In the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Mr. Dario Kordic had the role of vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. You talked about the Croatian Republic as well. Did he perform any duties there too?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No. I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Arar, let us move on to the main subject, why you've actually been called to testify here before this Honourable Court. And that is an incident at the Kacuni checkpoint where you were present. Tell us, please, in your opinion, when did this happen and which direction were you going back from? Tell us about that in two or three words, and then we'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: It was between the 20th and 21st of January, 1993. We were returning from the direction of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Which road did you take, who was with you, and what had happened in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: We were returning from Travnik. This was HDZ and the SDA of both parties. As we were returning, Mr. Dario Kordic went to Busovaca, to his home, and we proceeded straight to Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When you say "we", what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I proceeded, as well as Mr. Kostroman and Mr. Miro Musa, who sat in the co-drivers seat on the right-hand side, whereas Mr. Kostroman sat in the back seat. We came to the entrance to Kacuni. We did not notice anything. When we came to an intersection where there is a mosque, that intersection leads straight to the Silos, that's where a checkpoint had been made of anti-tank mines, on the left- and on the right-hand side there were bunkers that were made of sandbags, and behind the bunkers were soldiers. When we approached, a young man walked up to us and stopped us. As soon as we stopped, two were on one side and two were on the other side. They said that we should turn right to the Silos. I looked into the rear-view mirror and I saw that there was a small convoy of the UNHCR. We took a bit of time there. I turned to the right, but I went a bit to the back as well, so I saw this convoy pass, and I saw the army, the Bosnian army, remove the mines because the convoy had to go to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Just a second, please. I do apologise for having interrupted you. Could you just give us a few details? These soldiers who had surrounded you, were they armed? Or tell us something about that.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: The soldiers who were around us were wounded [as interpreted]. They had long rifles, automatic rifles. I also saw two machine guns, and I saw an RPG. I was a bit familiar with it because I -- as I passed through this area, I saw that my face was a bit similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Oh, so you had seen this man before; is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did anyone ever tell you his name?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I heard later that his name was Delija. I never knew his first name, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Oh, so somebody told you that?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Well, yes. As we talked, somebody told me. I don't know who it was. Somebody told me that his surname was Delija.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: All right. Let us continue from where you stopped. You said that you were told to go towards the Silos, you stopped there, and what happened then?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Then two soldiers were on one side and two soldiers were on the other side. They pointed their rifles at us, and one of the soldiers said to Mr. Miro Musa to get out with his hands up. Also, the other one said the same thing. He also said, "The other one too." When we did that, they took our weapons. They only took one automatic rifle from us and a nine-millimetre pistol, a Browning pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Whose pistol was that?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: It was my very own pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Did you ask them something? Did you try to talk to them?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I asked this one man, who was on the right-hand side by Mr. Miro Musa, I said, "Friend, what do we need all of this for? We are going from a meeting now, where your leaders were too." And he said, "Friend, perhaps we do know each other, perhaps we don't. We got orders. We got orders from Zenica." I asked him, "All right, boy. Who did you get these orders from? How could you get orders when all of your people were in Travnik?" And now I'm quoting. He said, "We got orders from Mr. Dzemal Merdan."

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did he give you -- how should I put this? -- some kind of code-name for this action?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: This boy didn't tell me a thing. I heard from another person who was a bit older. He said, exactly, "The bird is in the cage," Bird number 2, at that. I think that Bird number 2 had to be a code-name for Mr. Kostroman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. So there was a verbal conversation there. You were asking what all of this was about and this went on for a while, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes. It went on for about ten minutes or so, until the convoy left for Sarajevo. I heard all sorts of things being said: "Kill them. The Ustashas should be killed." I also heard -- how shall I put this? I heard a man who was drunk or whatever, and he was singing the following song: "From Sarajevo to Kupreska Vrata [phoen] There will be neither any Serbs nor Croats." Later on, when there seemed to be even more trouble, I looked into the other direction. I saw two vehicles coming from Busovaca. In the first vehicle -- I saw that this was a vehicle from Tisovac. In the first vehicle I saw Bogdan. I don't know the surnames exactly. I'll give you their first names. I saw Bogdan, I saw this -- Bogdan. I cannot remember all the names. I know Bogdan was there, and Milenko, Milenko Arapovic, and another one in the first vehicle. And in the second vehicle, I saw a man whose name I don't know. I just know his nickname. Krezo is his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: When they saw that these vehicles had arrived, there was panic. The gentleman nicknamed Krezo said, "[Realtime transcript read in error "jerks"], if you do not release Mr. Kostroman, my car is full of explosives; we are going to blow everything and everything up, and we are all going to die." In a very short period of time, Mr. Kostroman was released.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there appears to be a typographical error at line 21 of page 14. I think the word "gentlemen" was used and not the word that appears there. I'm sorry, Your Honour. It's line 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Please go ahead, Mr. Kostroman [as interpreted]. Please continue. You said that this man nicknamed Krezo said that he would activate the explosive and --

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Mr. Mira Musa and I got into the car and we set off. Our car was first, and these two other cars, one was from Tisovac and one was from the civilian police, as far as I can remember. We continued our drive to Kiseljak. We reached a cafe about two or three kilometres from the checkpoint where we had been stopped. We sat there for about an hour and a half or two, and from there we proceeded straight to Kresevo. We arrived in Kresevo around 10.30, 10.30, or 2230 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Are you sure about the number of vehicles that came from the direction of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I'm sure. I'm sure I saw two vehicles. I did not see any others.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please: On that occasion, at that checkpoint, apart from the vehicle that you, Mr. Kostroman, and your colleague Mira Musa were in, at this moment when you were halted, was there any other vehicle going with you?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please: Was Mr. Kordic stopped at that checkpoint together with Mr. Kostroman?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: He was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You have heard about the contention that on that occasion Mr. Kordic was also stopped at that checkpoint, not only you, but when you were allegedly moving from the direction of Kiseljak towards Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you're affirming what you just said a moment ago, that you were coming from the opposite direction?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I should like to adduce an exhibit at this point. Yesterday the question was asked if there was any trace in writing about the incident that took place on that occasion at Kacuni. It is a report entitled "Report on Incidents in the Area of Central Bosnia," dated 23rd January, 1993, and it was written and signed by the commander of the 4th Battalion of the military police in Vitez and addressed to the Operative Zone Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, will you take up the Croatian version, that is, the latter part of this exhibit, and will you please look who it is addressed to and who is signed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be marked D214.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this was an exhibit which was used in Blaskic case, and there it was marked D503.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You saw who signed this document. Will you please tell the Court, do you know who Pasko Ljubicic was?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Mr. Pasko Ljubicic was the commander of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In Vitez, you mean?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: In Vitez, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So in this -- in the first part, if you had an opportunity to look at it, where the municipality of Busovaca is mentioned, this incident is mentioned that Mr. Kostroman was stopped there, that this checkpoint -- let me sum it up briefly -- that this checkpoint was removed at a later stage and that some incidents are mentioned that happened that night in the town of Busovaca, and this seems to corroborate what you just said.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: This document is fully correct, but this is the first time I see this document. I did not know that it existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. So you were not the source of the information or the author of this document?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, please. We are now coming to the end. While Mr. Kostroman and Mr. Kordic worked at Tisovac, you spent most of your time at Tisovac and you were also a driver, so you will know which were the vehicles that Mr. Kostroman and Mr. Kordic used; you know which vehicles were parked there in front of the mansion that you lived and worked in?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was a Mercedes, then an Opel. There was a Renault 17, I think, and there were some other vehicles, but they were broken. For instance, there were some Golf vehicles and others, but they were broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, if Mr. Kordic or Mr. Kostroman ever used a Jeep.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No, never, because we did not have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And as you travelled around that area when you escorted Mr. Kostroman, did you ever see a Jeep with a white eagle painted on it?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you never saw such a Jeep in the area that you used to cover?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No. Only Colonel Tiho Blaskic had a Jeep, but even on it there were no eagles or any emblems. All that there was were HVO plates.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Arar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have concluded my examination-in-chief. You will now be asked questions by the Prosecution. Are you all right? Can you go on? Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, have you any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I was doing something else. No, I don't have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, who prepared the summary from which you're reading today?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe the witness was reading from any summary. That's a misleading question. He doesn't have any summary before him, in concordance with the Court's instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The first question should be: "Do you have a summary in front of you?"

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I shall rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, just a moment.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who prepared the summary that was given to the Prosecution today? Or yesterday, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I wrote it roughly in my own hand, and the lawyer then typed it for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You personally included in that all the information about yourself you wanted this Court to know; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: It is, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: There is a point where you indicate that the source of your knowledge is because you were in the inner circle. I shall point it out to the Judges. It's escaping me, but you referred to yourself as being in the inner circle with Mr. Kordic. Why, as an escort or a driver, would you consider yourself to be in the inner circle with Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I did not mean that I was the closest person to Dario Kordic. I was with Mr. Kostroman, and Mr. Kostroman was my superior.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Paragraph 27, you did say: "Mr. Kordic was not at the checkpoint at any time on the 20th or 21st of January or thereafter. I know this because I was in the inner circle of staff members at Mr. Kordic's and Mr. Kostroman's headquarters." Are you suggesting you did not have a close, confidant-type relationship with Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I have known Mr. Kordic since 1991. We were not on particular -- there was no particularly close relationship between us. It was simply business. If Mr. Kordic needed something from me, then he would say so to Mr. Kostroman, and Mr. Kostroman would then tell me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What kind of business?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Well, say if he needed a car, if one had to get fuel for his car, or bring food for the cooks, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In 1991? Food for the cooks in 1991? What cooks?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I didn't mean '91 for the cooks, I meant '93.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I see. How long -- excuse me. You said in your statement, your summary, that you have known Mr. Kostroman all your life. How did you meet Mr. Kostroman?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I knew him since my childhood. We played together, we played football together, because we come from two neighbouring municipalities. He played football in his municipality, and I played it in my municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The neighbouring municipalities being Kresevo and Kiseljak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you know Tihomir Blaskic all your life?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And he was from Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You and Mr. Kostroman are very, very close, are you not?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, I just want to make sure I understand correctly about why you are in the inner circle. Is that because you are a driver and an escort?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I think you were a very modest man. It seems that you have omitted all the biographical data about your being the head of the HDZ Kiseljak, which is a recognised fact. Is there a reason that you don't want to bring this up?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: As regards the Kiseljak HDZ, I was one of the first to form the HDZ in Kiseljak. I was one of the vice-presidents of the HDZ. That was in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Well, when did you stop being active in the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I stopped in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Then throughout the entire formative period of the Croatian Community and the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, you were not only a member of the HDZ, you were, in fact, the leader in Kiseljak; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I don't know what the word "leader" means. I was one of the vice-presidents, and that was in '91. When I had time, I attended meetings, but those meetings were very rare because I was too busy with Mr. Kostroman.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What were you doing for Mr. Kostroman in 1991 and '92?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Well, we went to Sarajevo together, to the main headquarters of the Bosnia-Herzegovinian HDZ. For a while, I was both with the security and one of the drivers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would like the usher to distribute, please, Exhibit Z1364.7. I believe it is a new exhibit. We probably can also do Z1177.1. I'm sorry, I have trouble reading the marking. Sorry, 1177.1 has been previously introduced. If the Registry would be kind enough to please pull it out. If I may, with the Court's permission, go ahead and begin to look at 1364.7.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: This is a document from BH command. Actually, it's out of Zagreb. It's for UNPROFOR. They tend to put into their who's whos only people whose positions are of significance for them, either as contacts, or for intelligence, or for some political or military reason. Now, I notice your name on the second page of it. In the left-hand column, it says: "Arar, Ivo", and then "Kiseljak CCHB". That must be "Croatian Community of --" it's probably "Bosna Herceg" just reversed. Could you explain how your name got into this particular directory, which is pretty selective?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, that's not for him to say. What you can ask is this: Mr. Arar, it appears from this that UNPROFOR thought that you were important enough to put into their directory of authorities or individuals in February 1994. Can you assist as to why they may have thought that? Obviously, you can't tell us why they did something, but can you think of any reason why they should have put you in this directory?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You've heard the Judge's question, Mr. Arar. Could you be kind enough to answer it?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is the first time I see this document, and I really don't know why my name appears here. I think that it could be perhaps only because I was one of the HDZ vice-presidents in the Kiseljak municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If we take a look at Z1177.1, if the usher could perhaps put it on the ELMO, and I'm really interested in identifying it initially than just looking at one page. Excuse me, Mr. Usher. That is the milinfosum? Mine is slightly set up a little different. Yes, okay. Your Honours, I'm hopeful I have the same copy, but what this is is a milinfosum dated 24 August 1993, and what I would like to point -- or ask Mr. Arar about is the entry on what is my very last page, which describes "Orbats/personalities". It said: "A request from Mate Boban for transport to a meeting to discuss the Geneva protocols reveals the Croat political hierarchy in Central Bosnia. The list, with appointment, is as follows: And there is a list which has "Dario Kordic" at the top. I think this is -- I'm sorry. Apparently what you have been given is a more limited edition. May I share with the Court my copy and put it on the ELMO. I think you have a bit of a watered-down one. Mr. Usher, could I ask you, please, to take my copy? I'm sorry for the inconvenience. It should have been an identical document. The last page, please. If you want to show the first page just so that it's possible to identify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, Exhibit Z1171.1 is not a milinfosum. It comes from the ECMM, and it's a two-page document and it doesn't have any attachments to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I can explain the glitch. I'm sorry, but there was a glitch on the part of our OTP which mismarked it. It should be 1179, and I do apologise. That is, in fact, a milinfosum. It's just simply mismarked on my copy. Again, I ask -- I'm terribly sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Having looked at the basis for the entry of a number of names, your name --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: A moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Surely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I have it. Yes. Let the witness have it, and look at the last page. Mr. Arar, do you read English at all?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, you'll see your name on the last page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, the list of names which Mr. Mate Boban gave to UNPROFOR is on the back. Do you see your name as number "R" or letter "R"? It says: "Ivo Arar, Kiseljak." Is that you?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Arar, in the early part of 1991, when the HDZ party was gaining momentum, you attended a number of meetings. And we won't spend an inordinate amount of time certainly on this, but just some of the highlights of the meetings at which you were present might help us understand a little bit about your role. Looking at Exhibit Z7, Z11, Z30, and Z41, I think all of these are in, as well as some meetings from 1992, Z18.1, and also Z2787, which is a photograph, I'd like to just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's have a look at the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Surely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What number is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The photograph, Your Honour, is number 2787.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is this a photograph of? Can you help us with it, Ms. Somers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is Mr. Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This photograph was introduced through the testimony of Stjepan Tuka, and this is a meeting of some of the representatives of the HDZ-BiH in the presidential palace, with Franjo Tudjman. Among these persons is Mr. Arar. He's in the back. If you look at the female, he would be to her right in the back. A younger Mr. Arar, but Mr. Arar nonetheless.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we better ask Mr. Arar first whether he recognises himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, you have heard the question of the judge. Can you confirm --

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And did you attend that meeting in the capacity of the driver for Mr. Kostroman or his escort?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were there other drivers invited to be photographed with President Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No. I was the vice-president of the HDZ of Kiseljak at that time, because Mr. Jozo Boro could not come with us, so I was told to go instead, and Mr. Kostroman together with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That was in June of 1991. Now, if we look at Z7, please, which is a meeting -- excuse me one second -- of July 21, 1991, do you see --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Is it in front of the witness yet? I guess not. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you see your name as those in attendance at this meeting of the HDZ? After the name Marijan Skopljak, do you see your name?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you recall this meeting?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So you would have to read the minutes to refresh your memory about the meeting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And would this meeting, would the minutes of this meeting reflect every item that was discussed and every vote that was taken?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The person who was the administrative secretary who signed off on these minutes, along with Dario Kordic, as the chairman of that meeting, was Ignac Kostroman, your friend. Was it your understanding that your friend accurately recorded all the meeting minutes, every vote, dissenting and affirming?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I would not know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Just a couple of points, since you don't seem to have an independent recollection of things, but there were some comments that were made, and I wonder if you could just tell us if you agree with them. There was a comment, for example, discussing the following: "Because of the loss of confidence in the HDZ in some areas, there are attempts to establish other Croatian parties with more radical goals." Do you remember that? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I don't know that. I did not write this. Yes, I was present, but I did not write it. This is the first time I see these minutes, this record here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: "There is also discontent with some members of the presidency that is being raised." Did you feel discontent with some members of the presidency? That would have been Stjepan Kljuic and the members of his slate.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: As for me, I was quite happy with everybody. I was not a politician. That is, I was a politician only in Kiseljak, and only in the HDZ party. And as for the top, nothing; I only went as a driver. Nobody asked my opinion there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can we please turn to Z11, which is 13 August 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You have it in front of you? This particular meeting had present Mate Boban, and again the minutes were signed off by -- sorry to fumble here -- by your friend, Ignac Kostroman, and also listing the chairpersons as Mate Boban, Martin Udovicic, and Dario Kordic. Now, this -- do you have any recollection of this meeting, what took place there? It was a fairly contentious meeting. Does that stick out in your memory?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I remember the meeting, but I was not present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If you look at the first page of the agenda, maybe it's wrong, maybe your friend didn't mark it correctly, but it does say, first page: "Present at the session, under Kiseljak, Josip Boro, Marko Frankovic ..." And what's the third name there? Is it Ivo Arar?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I think this is a mistake. I did come, but I drove Mr. Kostroman there and I didn't attend this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So you, as the representative of the HDZ Kiseljak, waited outside, in your dual role as driver, while a very important meeting with Mate Boban took place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Vice-president. I was not president. Vice-president. The third one, at that. Vice-president.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I said "representative". But whatever your role, vice-president is -- you consider that insignificant?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I do not, but I don't think that it is necessary to have two or three men from one place. The only role that I played was that of driver over there. As for the rest of them, they did what they had to do at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Well, at this point, Mate Boban was also just a vice-president. He was Mr. Kljuic's vice-president, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: At this meeting, there is a lot of criticism of Mr. Kljuic, who I don't believe was there. Did you voice any concern? You told us earlier that you were very happy with everything about the HDZ. Did you voice any concern about some of these extremely unflattering things that are said about Mr. Kljuic? For example -- excuse me, I don't mean to cut you off before you answer, but let me just ask you in connection with this question. Point number 3 of the decisions --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe Mr. Naumovski has risen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do apologise, but I feel the need to say this. Mr. Arar said that he was in the HDZ, and he said that he was vice-president of the municipal organisation of the HDZ in Kiseljak. However, everything that he is being asked now absolutely goes beyond the reasons why Mr. Arar was brought here as a witness. Now he's being asked about his opinions of Mr. Kljuic, Mr. Boban, et cetera. This definitely goes beyond the direct examination. Mr. Arar said that he was one of the founders of the HDZ. That's all. I don't see why one should go this broadly. Thank you. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's relevant to credibility, but no doubt it can be done as expeditiously as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I shall certainly try. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May I just quickly quote to you: "The behaviour of Stjepan Kljuic, president of the HDZ-BiH, while conducting the session of the HDZ-BiH main board on 6 August 1991, is judged as unbefitting and unacceptable. He skilfully managed to avert discussion on the decisions of Travnik Regional Community, although his attention was several times directed to the material on hand and the agenda adopted." And then following that it says: "We hereby call on President Stjepan Kljuic to explain his behaviour at a meeting of the HDZ-BiH presidency. The explanation will then be passed --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: "The explanation will then be passed on to the regional community." Did you consider yourself or did you list yourself in any kind of vote among those who said, "We hereby call on president Stjepan Kljuic to do..." what I just read?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you voice any opposition in as much as you told us that you were very happy with the HDZ? I do not see opposition here. Did someone fail to write down your opposing vote?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about all of this here. I wouldn't really comment too much about this. I really do not know whether there were conflicts, and obviously there were, according to this evidence. I think there is nothing for me to say in relation to this. There was no vote; that I know for sure. Replacements were normal, as agreed by Mr. Mate Boban and Mr. Stjepan Kljuic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know Martin Udovicic?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I do, but very superficially.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You don't know him well enough to know, then, that his name is listed at the bottom of the minutes as well. Would it surprise you to learn that he also didn't have any opposing vote cast or recorded -- I'm sorry -- recorded, that he shared a very positive view about Mr. Kljuic that you claim you had, and that his opposition to this was not recorded either? Would that surprise you?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Next exhibit, please, which would be January 27th, 1992. I'm sorry. I beg your pardon. 28 November, Z30.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, I do not know, in fairness, if you were at this meeting, and that is not why I have this exhibit in front of you. We do know that Ante Beljo, from Zagreb, was at the meeting, but if you would turn to item 2, point D, which in the English is on page 3. It says: "A commission consisting of Andjelka Stojic, Matilda Dragicevic, and Ivo Arar is hereby appointed to take an inventory of the fixed assets and small inventory in use as of 31 December 1991." What type of inventory was this really? Can you describe what you actually had to do? Did you fulfil this task?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I fulfilled this task. These were two computers, one photocopier, and then also inventory for catering. This was at the headquarters of the HDZ in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Next exhibit, please, Z41.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, these are minutes, or excerpts from minutes of a meeting of the Travnik Subregional Community of Herceg-Bosna from 27 January 1992, and I see in the portion on the first page, where it says "attended by", your name, it says: "Ivo Arar, Kiseljak." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you remember this meeting?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What makes you remember this meeting over all the other meetings that we've discussed? What took place there that sticks out in your mind?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Because I went on behalf of Kiseljak, as the vice-president of the HDZ, to attend this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And at that meeting there were a number of discussions, among them the upcoming referendum for BiH independence. This meeting, of course -- let's see now. Who signed off on this? This was signed off on by Dario Kordic, with your friend Ignac Kostroman taking the minutes. And one question I'd like to ask you about, in point 6, please. "We state that inter parte negotiations up to now have been consciously obstructed by Stjepan Kljuic, and this subregion ..." headed by Dario Kordic -- that's parentheses, my comment, of course, "... withdraws any right bestowed on him for representing the party and the Croatian people." Did you agree to this?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The next exhibit -- excuse me one second -- a document which has not yet been tendered, so I would ask for distribution, would be Z252.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's apparently in the outstanding exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm sorry for the confusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, this document, dated 24 October, 1992, is an informational document which summarises some negotiations in Sarajevo, directed to the Mostar Main Staff for Bozo Rajic and for the IPD, the Information/Propaganda/Intel folks. Now, your name is mentioned as being part of that delegation. Do you remember being part of that delegation? At the bottom it said: "The members of our delegation were," and it has: "Tihomir Blaskic, Ignac Kostroman, Marko Prskalo, Ante Sliskovic and Ivo Arar". Do you recall being there on the 23rd of October?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I remember this document, but I did not attend this. At that time, I was in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How did your name get down there as being present? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Very gladly. This document was made five days before I was supposed to go to Germany.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It was made five days before you were supposed to go to Germany. But this records an event that took place on the 23rd of October. Now, when did you go to Germany?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I went on the 25th.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So you're saying you weren't there, but your name is here. Now, there were some significant things that occurred. If you were not there and these things are attributed to you as a member of the delegation, did you write a letter to correct this, to show that you were not a member of the delegation?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I didn't write anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: This was just -- did you hear about what happened at this particular meeting where your delegation demanded the removal, as a condition of any further negotiations, the removal of Refik Lendo from Novi Travnik? Were you aware of that, that your name was under that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I didn't hear a thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Excuse me just a minute. You've indicated that as far as you know, Dario Kordic never had any particular role in picking the members of any military unit. Now, that was not an area within one of your many competencies, was it? You were not handling the selection of military persons, were you?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You were not handling them or, yes, you were handling them?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No, no, no, it was not my duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So you really don't know what Dario Kordic may or may not have done about the selection of anything; that was simply not part of your -- it was not within your portfolio; correct? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, Tisovac. There has been quite a bit of evidence about where Mr. Kordic had his offices, and I just wanted to ask you if you can indicate whether or not a building called Sumarija, which is, I believe, translated as "forestry office" -- is that correct? It has to do with wood or forestry; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would you explain that? Could you correct me, please?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I can explain. The office of Mr. Dario Kordic was in Tisovac, and it was called Plave Salon, the Blue Parlour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: But "Sumarija", what is that all about? What does that actually mean? It's come up with a number of UNPROFOR witnesses and members of the International Community. What is a Sumarija?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Sumarija, that is a building. I don't know. The brigade, Nikola Subic-Zrinjski, was located there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: But the term refers to what type of industry? Does it refer to farming, does it refer to fire brigades; what type of industry is the Sumarija?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Sumarija, those are offices of the Sumarija. How can I explain this to you? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Does that concern forestry, which is one of the government industries, forestry? Just tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I guess so. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, you are now living in Knin; is that correct? That's what you said in your report?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw Ignac Kostroman?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: The last time I saw him, it was about two months ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I saw him in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Is he living in Knin?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: From time to time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And from time to time, where else does he live?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: In Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Is his family with him?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Some are, others aren't, because one child attends school in Zagreb, and another child is sick and is in Zagreb in hospital, and one child and his wife are in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would like to ask you about Germany. You left Germany, you said, in 1980, but you also indicated you've made trips back to Germany since. You indicated you were on your way to Germany when the Mixed Military Working Group session in '92 took place. What type of activity did you engage in in Germany after you returned to live permanently in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I only went to Germany for private matters. I have four brothers still living in Germany. I never went to Germany to have meetings organised or something like that. I went to Germany straight to see my brothers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you -- well, you yourself mentioned meetings. I'm a little curious about that. I hadn't said anything quite yet, but there is a meeting of the -- the minutes of a meeting that I have looked at and which I would be happy to put on the ELMO. I'm not seeking to introduce it, by any stretch. But it's from Stuttgart, and it's from the 9th of November, 1991, and it's a meeting of the exiles, essentially, of the Croat emigres from Kresevo and Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May I ask the usher simply to put it on the ELMO for all of us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Somers, how is this going to assist us?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The content of it, Your Honour. I'm going to ask him about what he was doing in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can you comment? Can you see it okay? Can you just tell us what you were doing there? Were you doing work on behalf of the HDZ-BiH when you were in Germany? I'm looking actually at it looks like "G" sort of in the middle of that page above the name -- well, your name is there. It says: "Ivo Arar from Kiseljak, secretary of the HDZ." What were you actually doing there?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I went to Germany with the intention to stay with my brothers. I heard that presidents or vice-presidents would come from three municipalities to attend a meeting in Stuttgart. These are not emigres, these are men who live and work there and who collect money for the municipalities of Fojnica, Kiseljak and Kresevo so that people could buy flour there. I heard about that, and when they came, I went together with my four brothers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Flour. "Flour" like for bread flour or "flowers" like flowers?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, which one is it?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think we're going to get much further with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now it's getting on to the time for the adjournment, in any event. There's something I want to ask. Mr. Arar, you were asked questions about these documents, and what essentially was being put was this: that they tend to show or may show that you were part of the leadership of the HDZ and that you weren't simply a driver, an escort, for Mr. Kostroman, that you were playing a larger part in political events. Now, that's one possible interpretation of these documents. Can you assist us as to what the reality was? Were you simply a driver, an escort, or were you playing a part in the politics?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: My politics, the top rank I reached was vice-president of the municipal HDZ in Kiseljak. And I did two other jobs, driver and bodyguard for Mr. Kostroman; nothing else. I have to say the truth and nothing but the truth here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn now for half an hour. Ms. Somers, would you tailor your cross-examination after the adjournment, please? The witness isn't looking very well, and we need to finish his evidence as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, if you don't feel well after the adjournment, let us know. But you've got a break now for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Arar, I understand you weren't well during the adjournment. How are you feeling now?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I'm all right. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we will ensure that it's not for long. Ms. Somers, given the circumstances, I don't know if you were told that the witness was unwell during the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That is the position we've been told. I think we will try and curtail cross-examination as much as possible. Is there anything of importance which you ought to put?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm sorry. I didn't mean to interrupt you. If I could respond to your telling me about curtailing. There are some important points. I am very sympathetic to the physical condition, but I must, perhaps even in the most brief way, raise certain points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And including issues from the affidavits which are submitted. Now, because I speak fast anyway, I can speak a little faster, and if the interpreters can follow, we can go through those very quickly, but they must be discussed. And there are some very specific points about the checkpoint incident. I will try to be brief, but I must emphasise that this is very critical evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if you could come to the checkpoint, I think, and deal with that quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If I can ask -- I was on the tail of the last question about the Stuttgart document, and I will quickly put it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, there has been evidence given to this Tribunal by a number of people, including Stjepan Tuka, that Ignac Kostroman and Bruno Susnjar were collecting money, were fund-raising for the HVO, or the Herceg-Bosna, rather, effort, and that fund-raising was aimed specifically at the purchase of weapons. Tell us, please: What you were doing in Stuttgart was related directly to fund-raising for the purchase of weapons, as has been indicated by the testimony to which I have referred; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Looking at the incident in Kacuni at the checkpoint, I'd like to get a little bit of a better understanding about what you were doing in Travnik that day. Now, you are a political person, as you have admitted to this court, and as a political person, if you were attending a meeting of the SDA and the HDZ in Travnik, you should know the name of the president of the SDA in Travnik. Can you tell us who that was, please?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did not attend the meeting. I said that I was a vice-president of the HDZ in the municipality of Kiseljak, but I was not present at the meeting. I drove Mr. Ignac Kostroman to the meeting and I waited for the meeting to end, and when it did, we went home.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you saying, then, that you, a vice-president of the HDZ Kiseljak, went to a meeting in a very volatile environment, which meeting was a joint meeting of the SDA and the HDZ, and you waited outside because you were driving; you were the escort? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And who was the head of the -- the representative for the SDA in Travnik whom Mr. Kostroman and Mr. Kordic were visiting? Name, please.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You had never, in the course of dealing -- as part of the Travnik Regional Community, you had never had dealings with the SDA in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I never had a meeting arranged with the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I didn't ask you about a meeting; I asked you for a name, the name of the head of the SDA in Travnik with whom Mr. Kordic and Mr. Kostroman were meeting.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I've already told you: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, you know that there are no meetings at all of the SDA and the HDZ any time in 1993, were there, in Travnik, none at all?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: That's what you say, and I say that there was a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What was the address at which this meeting that you dropped your friend and Mr. Kordic off? Can you give us the address in Travnik, please?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: The meeting was held in the building of Sumarija of the forestry management.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the report by the Spanish Battalion which, because it is in Spanish, I will spare the Court at this point from having to deal with the translation? It talks about the general conditions in Central Bosnia on those days during the period of time in question. Are you aware of the tensions in Vitez and the tensions in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I am not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You were not aware. And you drove through the areas that were documented by the Spanish Battalion as -- excuse my need to translate from Spanish, but reading on the -- and I quote, you, and you can tell me if you heard about this. It is a Spanish Battalion document dated 23 January 1993, and it describes the condition in Central Bosnia. It says: "On the 19th of January, we were informed that Muslim civilians from Vitez had been --" excuse me. "In Vitez, Travnik and Novi Travnik, the HVO ordered the Bosnian, the Bosniaks, to lay down their arms." And a subsequent entry says: "In Travnik, those Bosnian refused to lay down their arms, as ordered by the HVO." Were you aware of the particular tension that was existing during this time period on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: They did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was it your custom to check conditions, before you escorted your friend and Mr. Kordic to a place, for their own security?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: For me, there was security, because the road was not blocked anywhere. It is quite true that there was some tension, a little, but mainly in Travnik between Serbs on one side and us Croats and the Muslims on the other, because at that time we had our joint defence against Serbs. As for those in Novi Travnik, I know nothing about laying down of weapons, I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You mentioned in your evidence, or your evidence was, that a roadblock or a checkpoint appeared, you came across a checkpoint. When did you first learn that the checkpoint at Kacuni had been erected?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: When I reached the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were you -- I'd just like to read you a passage and actually show you and the Court Z391.2, a milinfosum spanning from 15 to 21 January 1993. If I may ask the usher to distribute it, please. This milinfosum from UNPROFOR headquarters covers the period -- it is a sitrep of all sectors dated from 15 to 21 January, so the conditions described herein are valid at least to the 21st of January. Turning to page 11, there are entries for 19 January, and then it is evident it is a typo. It says "10 January", but it is couched between 19 and 21 January, so clearly it is the 20th of January. Entry number 3: "Busovaca. BiH forces have set up a new roadblock in Kacuni, south-east of Busovaca, on the road from Kiseljak to Vitez." This condition existed from at least the 20th of January, at least, and we have had evidence that it existed earlier and was in place until the end of the period covered by this sitrep, which is the 21st of January, 1993. Can you explain, please, the entry -- can you explain, please, how you did not know about it?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I can. Every morning, Mr. Kostroman and I would come to Busovaca from Kresevo, Kiseljak, and that is one of the reasons which I can offer you to show that there was no checkpoint. I do not really know when was it that it happened to us, whether it was the 20th or the 21st. It was the first time that the roadblock was erected, at least to my knowledge, as far as I know. I affirm -- I contend that there were no roadblocks before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You seem now to be able to pin it down to the 20th or the 21st. May I ask you, how many times have you been stopped at roadblocks with Mr. Kostroman where he has been the object, as you say, of such action by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Well, about five times.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So there are other incidents where Mr. Kostroman has been stopped. And Mr. Kordic as well, have you ever been stopped in the company of Mr. Kordic on other occasions where the BH army has made such --

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry? Did you hear my question, and what was your answer?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: "No." New question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Arar, the description that you gave of the order of --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. With your leave, Your Honours, I think the transcript is not quite correct. The witness asked to be repeated the question. I sit very near him. He did not say, "New question," but he wanted the question to be repeated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I think it's been answered satisfactorily. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Arar, Defence counsel has presented today a document, D214/1, which details an event occurring on the 20th of January, and it appears it is at a checkpoint, and are you aware whether -- is it possible -- have you looked at the document? Is it possible, after having read it, that there might have been more than one incident on the 20th of January -- does that strike you as possible -- where this could have happened?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I know only about the incident which happened on the 20 and or the 21st. I cannot tell you exactly when it did happen, whether it was the 20th or the 21st. As for other incidents, if there were any, I really do not know anything about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So you're not sure whether the document shown by Defence counsel today discusses the incident which we are discussing in this courtroom; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: And what do I answer to this question? I am telling you, I had almost nothing to do with documents. I was a simple driver who was ordered to go somewhere and bring something back. That was the description of my job.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: But we do agree that this document is crystal clear about the date. It says "20 January", does it not?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, the summary which you submitted and the evidence which you gave today says -- let me see now. I don't want to get it wrong. Point 17 of your summary: "On either January 20th or 21st, 1993." Do you always have that -- allow for a gap of a day or so when you plan things or when you make your schedule, or have you ever missed an appointment because you thought it was one day and it was the next?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is the sort of point -- you've made the point, Ms. Somers. It's the sort of point which we can, in all circumstances, take quickly. We have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you if you remember -- well, some other persons who claim to have been at the scene have submitted their versions of events, and I'd just like to ask you if these sound correct to you, if I could, please. They've done it in written form. They have not come to court, for whatever reason. Before I move on to that, I would like to just ask you one quick question. Are you aware that on the -- of critical issues occurring -- tensions occurring in Busovaca on January 20th or 21st, where the bank was blown up, the Privedna Bank was blown up in the Muslim section?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that the bank explosion occurred in another place, not Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I meant "Vitez". I beg your pardon. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you familiar with that event?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'd just like to take one quick minute and ask the usher, unless it's in, Z386.1, to just show this to you and see if it rings a bell. Perhaps the usher might put it on the ELMO. This is an announcement made by the executive board of the SDA in Vitez, the same party that Mr. Kordic and Mr. Kostroman, you claim, were visiting, although that was in Travnik. And it simply says that: "Last night in Vitez, 20 January 1993, at about 2200 hours, a very strong explosive device demolished the offices of Privedna Banka in Travnik, located in downtown Vitez, which is under the control of the HVO formations." And it talks about: "The Muslim people in our community are embittered by the pressure exerted on them from brutal threats," and it moves on to describe the fact that the Privedna Banka Zagreb, which is only 50 metres away, was left intact.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you aware of this, all these events of the 20th?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I'm not aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Several affidavits were submitted, as I have mentioned earlier, by persons by the name of Brano Kristo, Milenko -- let me get his last name -- Arapovic, I think it is. Yes, Milenko Arapovic. And the third one is -- sorry. I've got to try to get that together -- Bogdan Santic. Do you know these names?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were these people who were supposedly involved also in some way or another at the checkpoint incident on the 20th of January at Kacuni?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I think that one -- no, two were, and the third one was not. Franjo [as interpreted] Kristo was not involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Let me just tell you what one of them said, and see if you can tell me if this is correct. And I will try to go quickly. One of them said: "On 20th or 21st January, 1993, I accompanied Mr. Kordic and Mr. Kostroman as they were attending talks with representatives of the SDA."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you slow down, Ms. Somers, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: "We were returning from Travnik to Busovaca through Busovaca through Vitez."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I was just told that -- I beg your pardon. The transcript says "Franjo Kristo". It was Brano Kristo. If that can be corrected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, the witness said he did not know Franjo Kristo, that he was not there, because he understood that he was being asked about Franjo Kristo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, let's get this straight. Look, rather than doing it the other way around, what the witness should be asked is positive questions. Ms. Somers, don't read out part of the affidavit and ask him to comment. He's merely commenting on what somebody said. If there is a discrepancy, of course, you can ask him about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, would you tell us, please, Mr. Arar, who was in the cars and who was involved in this incident which you've described at Kacuni on your side.

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: There were myself, Mr. Kostroman, Mr. Miro Musa, Milenko Arapovic, Damir Cosic, Brano, "Krezo." I don't know his last name. I can't recall all names but there were other people too. I don't really know all the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, you were asked earlier: Was Franjo Kristo involved? What is the answer to that?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: He was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, was Brano Kristo involved, if I can get a clarification on that?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry for the confusion, Mr. Arar. There is another name that appeared in the document that was presented by Defence counsel, and I will come to ask you about that name in a moment as well. Can you just tell us, please, how many walkie-talkies were involved in the -- or Motorolas, if you might call them that -- were involved in the incident? Do you know? On the part of the HVO personnel, who had a Motorola among your group?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Our group had two Motorolas.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And who had them, please? Which persons?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: I had one, and one was in the vehicle with Mr. Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And which of the three names that you just gave -- Kristo, Arapovic, or Santic -- was with Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: With Dario Kordic, in Travnik, were both -- were also from the civilian police, except that I don't know their names. And with Dario were Milenko Arapovic and those other two. I can't remember the names.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who, according to your version of things, who drove Mr. Kordic home? Which of the three were with Mr. Kordic when he went home to Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: The car was driven by Milenko Arapovic, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And where was Brano Kristo? With whom was he?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Brano Kristo, I don't know whose car he was in. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Just tell me if this is correct. You said there were two cars that came from the direction of Busovaca to the checkpoint that you could see; is that correct, two cars?

utterances.speaker: IVO ARAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
